result.stdout:
idrak: Idrak's command-line tool

Usage: idrak COMMAND [arguments] [options]

Setup and health:
  doctor (doc)                  What works on this machine and what to fix: runtime, backends, devices, caches, disk,
                                environment
  devices (dev)                 Every device: backend, name, memory, compute units, subgroup size, matrix units,
                                kernel width
  version                       Versions of the tool, the libraries, the .NET runtime and the device drivers
  report                        A report (Markdown and JSON) of the machine, devices, drivers, tests and benchmarks
  env (environment)             Every environment variable Idrak reads: value, default and meaning
  env set                       Save environment variables for every idrak run, in any terminal (asks for them, with
                                suggested values)
  env unset                     Remove environment variables saved by idrak env set
  env reset                     Remove every saved environment variable: all back to their defaults (asks first)
  init                          Writes the config file: default device, cache folder, model aliases
  cache info                    Sizes and paths of the caches (models, tuning, kernels, downloads)
  cache clear                   Clears one part of the cache (models, tuning, kernels) or all of it
  config get                    Prints a config value (dotted keys, e.g. aliases.qwen.model)
  config set                    Sets a config value (JSON values such as ["a.dll"] or 4 are kept as JSON)
  config unset                  Removes a config value
  config list                   Every config value (or a profile's), and the file's path
  plugins list                  Everything registered: formats, families, RoPE scalings, tool-call formats, ops,
                                devices
  formats                       Every registered weight, KV cache, checkpoint, dataset and tool-call format
  completion                    Prints a

result.stdout:
idrak convert: Convert between GGUF and Hugging Face folders (safetensors bf16, f16, f32)

Usage: idrak convert IN OUT [--type bf16|f16|f32] [-f] [--dry-run]

Arguments:
  IN   a .gguf file, a model folder, a cached Hugging Face id or an alias
  OUT  a folder: the model in the Hugging Face layout (model.safetensors, config, tokenizer, template)

Options:
  -o, --out DIR  OUT as an option
      --type T   the element type of the written weights (default bf16)
  -f, --force    write into a folder that is not empty
      --dry-run  say what would be written

GGUF weights are dequantized (float32 in memory, one model at a time) and written in --type.

Examples:
  idrak convert ./qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf ./qwen3-0.6b
  idrak convert Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B -o ./qwen-f32 --type f32

Gaps: writing GGUF files (the library reads GGUF but has no writer) and language models as .ikm packages (a
package holds a network built from a builder description; a pretrained decoder is not loaded from one yet).

Common options:
  -d, --device NAME   cpu, cuda:0, vulkan:1, hip:0 (default: the default device)
  -P, --plugin PATH   load an assembly that registers formats, families, ... (repeatable)
  -j, --json          machine-readable output
  -q, --quiet         less output; -v, --verbose: more
      --cache DIR     the cache folder (default IDRAK_CACHE or ~/.cache/idrak)
  -C, --config FILE   the config file (default IDRAK_CONFIG or ~/.idrak/config.json)
      --log FILE      also write every line, verbose ones included, to FILE
      @FILE           read arguments from FILE, one per line (@@text: a literal @text)
  -O, --output FILE   write the command's main output to FILE
      --format F      text, json, csv or md (tables)
      --color WHEN    auto, always or never (NO_COLOR still wins); --plain: no Unicode or progress line
      --offline       use only what is cached; a download is an error
      --threads N     CPU threads; --seed N: one seed for sampling, shuffling and initialization
      --timeout D     give up after a duration (30s, 5
[truncated]

commands.payload:
idrak: Idrak's command-line tool

Usage: idrak COMMAND [arguments] [options]

Setup and health:
  doctor (doc)                  What works on this machine and what to fix: runtime, backends, devices, caches, disk,
                                environment
  devices (dev)                 Every device: backend, name, memory, compute units, subgroup size, matrix units,
                                kernel width
  version                       Versions of the tool, the libraries, the .NET runtime and the device drivers
  report                        A report (Markdown and JSON) of the machine, devices, drivers, tests and benchmarks
  env (environment)             Every environment variable Idrak reads: value, default and meaning
  env set                       Save environment variables for every idrak run, in any terminal (asks for them, with
                                suggested values)
  env unset                     Remove environment variables saved by idrak env set
  env reset                     Remove every saved environment variable: all back to their defaults (asks first)
  init                          Writes the config file: default device, cache folder, model aliases
  cache info                    Sizes and paths of the caches (models, tuning, kernels, downloads)
  cache clear                   Clears one part of the cache (models, tuning, kernels) or all of it
  config get                    Prints a config value (dotted keys, e.g. aliases.qwen.model)
  config set                    Sets a config value (JSON values such as ["a.dll"] or 4 are kept as JSON)
  config unset                  Removes a config value
  config list                   Every config value (or a profile's), and the file's path
  plugins list                  Everything registered: formats, families, RoPE scalings, tool-call formats, ops,
                                devices
  formats                       Every registered weight, KV cache, checkpoint, dataset and tool-call format
  completion                    Prints a

idrak convert: Convert between GGUF and Hugging Face folders (safetensors bf16, f16, f32)

Usage: idrak convert IN OUT [--type bf16|f16|f32] [-f] [--dry-run]

Arguments:
  IN   a .gguf file, a model folder, a cached Hugging Face id or an alias
  OUT  a folder: the model in the Hugging Face layout (model.safetensors, config, tokenizer, template)

Options:
  -o, --out DIR  OUT as an option
      --type T   the element type of the written weights (default bf16)
  -f, --force    write into a folder that is not empty
      --dry-run  say what would be written

GGUF weights are dequantized (float32 in memory, one model at a time) and written in --type.

Examples:
  idrak convert ./qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf ./qwen3-0.6b
  idrak convert Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B -o ./qwen-f32 --type f32

Gaps: writing GGUF files (the library reads GGUF but has no writer) and language models as .ikm packages (a
package holds a network built from a builder description; a pretrained decoder is not loaded from one yet).

Common options:
  -d, --device NAME   cpu, cuda:0, vulkan:1, hip:0 (default: the default device)
  -P, --plugin PATH   load an assembly that registers formats, families, ... (repeatable)
  -j, --json          machine-readable output
  -q, --quiet         less output; -v, --verbose: more
      --cache DIR     the cache folder (default IDRAK_CACHE or ~/.cache/idrak)
  -C, --config FILE   the config file (default IDRAK_CONFIG or ~/.idrak/config.json)
      --log FILE      also write every line, verbose ones included, to FILE
      @FILE           read arguments from FILE, one per line (@@text: a literal @text)
  -O, --output FILE   write the command's main output to FILE
      --format F      text, json, csv or md (tables)
      --color WHEN    auto, always or never (NO_COLOR still wins); --plain: no Unicode or progress line
      --offline       use only what is cached; a download is an error
      --threads N     CPU threads; --seed N: one seed for sampling, shuffling and initialization
